newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia Unibank to raise 50 bln rph from listing.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Unibank to raise 50 bln rph from listing.

text.p: Indonesian small-size PT United City Bank (Unibank) said on Thursday it expected to raise around 50 billion rupiah by offering a 34.15 percent stake, or 70 million shares, to the public in late May.
"The bank plans to offer 70 million shares with an initial offering price expected to be between 600 rupiah to 800 rupiah per share," president director Odang Kariana told reporters.
Kariana said the shares, with a nominal value of 500 rupiah per share, were expected to be listed on the Jakarta stock exchange in early June.

He said the bank expected to use 50 percent of the proceeds to boost its medium and long-term loan growth, 20 percent to expand its network, 25 percent to improve information systems and technology and the rest for human resources development.
Each annual dividend payment for the years 1997, 1998 and 1999 would amount to 21 percent of the initial public offering price, Kariana said.
The bank said the offer was an incentive for investors.

"If the bank's net profit is not enough to cover the dividend payment which amount to 21 percent of the IPO price, the founder shareholders will provide the needed funds to the investing public," Kariana said.
Unibank posted a net profit of 11.7 billion rupiah in 1996, or up 32.8 percent from the previous year.
It posted an unaudited pre-tax profit of 5.69 billion rupiah in the first quarter of this year. The bank did not give the comparative figures.
Kariana said the bank expected to book net profit growth of 31.5 percent in 1997.

Gunawan Jusuf, managing director of lead underwriter PT Makindo, said the price earnings ratio (PER) was likely to be between seven to nine times compared to an average current PER of between nine to ten times for other small banks.
